Title: Prospective Randomized Comparison of Valved Versus Nonvalved Peripherally Inserted Central Vein Catheters
Author: Hoffer et al.
Comment: The analysis unit is the catheter; some patients received multiple catheters. The Abstract conflicts with the main Results, reporting five valved occlusions and p = .06, while Table 5 and the detailed Results paragraph report six valved occlusions and p = .10. This row prioritizes the main Results/Table 5 as prespecified. The catheter groups also differed in flush solution and inner lumen diameter.

Report_ID: Catheter occlusion during PICC dwell time
Title: A prospective, randomized comparison of three different types of valved and non-valved peripherally inserted central catheters
Author: Mauro Pittiruti et al.
Comment: The paper does not present a single combined overall-occlusion cell for the requested two-group contrast. Event counts were formed from Table II by summing the explicitly reported mutually listed occlusion categories (irreversible, transient, and PWO): no valve 0+2+1=3; Solo valve 1+2+1=4; PASV 0+1+0=1. The two eligible valved arms were then combined: 4+1=5 events and 61+60=121 catheters. The analysis unit is PICC/catheter (one PICC per randomized patient). No exact p value, confidence interval, or relative effect estimate was reported in Results.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Non-valved ProPICC') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Prospective randomized controlled three-arm parallel-group trial
domain: Vascular access in adult oncology patients
Participant type: Adult oncologic patients receiving intermittent chemotherapy
Recruitment source: Day Hospital of Oncology, Catholic University Hospital, Rome
Outcome measurement: Number of PICCs/catheters with an irreversible occlusion, transient occlusion, or partial withdrawal occlusion (PWO) during dwell time, assessed using a nurse questionnaire at each catheter use
Outcome variable: Catheter occlusion during PICC dwell time

Title: A comparison of hydrophobic polyurethane and polyurethane peripherally inserted central catheter: results from a feasibility randomized controlled trial
Author: Gavin et al.
Comment: The Table 2 percentages (60% and 55%) use the numbers with any complication as their denominators, not the full randomized/analyzed arm totals, so they were not recorded as arm-level risks. Arm-level synthesis counts are 15/55 for the integrated-valve PICC and 11/55 for the no-valve PICC. Follow-up was capped at 4 weeks unless the PICC was removed earlier. The arms also differed in hydrophobic surface/material technology, so this comparison does not isolate the valve effect.
domain: Vascular access / peripherally inserted central catheters
Study Environment: Single quaternary hospital and Hospital in the Home service
Topic of Content: Integrated proximal-valve versus external-clamp PICC technology
Recruitment source: Patients consecutively recruited at the Royal Brisbane and Women’s Hospital Department of Medical Imaging
Outcome measurement: Number of patients experiencing occlusion during treatment; patient was the stated unit of measurement
